title: Prestwick adds fifth China cargo gateway
metaDescription: Glasgow Prestwick is in talks with Jiangsu to open a Nanjing cargo route in 2027, giving UK sellers a fifth Chinese airport option alongside Shanghai and…
bottomLine: Glasgow Prestwick and Jiangsu officials are negotiating a direct cargo route to Nanjing Lukou for 2027, which would give UK-bound sellers a fifth Chinese airport gateway. Nothing is signed and no operator is named. The only firm number is the 20 weekly China services Prestwick already handles.

stories.headline: Prestwick opens talks on fifth China cargo route, to Nanjing
stories.tldr: Glasgow Prestwick is negotiating a Nanjing Lukou cargo link for 2027, which would be its fifth Chinese airport connection.
stories.whatHappened:
Glasgow Prestwick Airport (PIK) has started talks with the Jiangsu Provincial Government about a direct cargo connection to Nanjing Lukou International Airport (NKG), with a possible launch in 2027. PIK chief executive Jules Matteoni and regional director Colin Dai met Jiangsu vice governor Ma Shiguang in Nanjing.

Prestwick already handles 20 China services a week and lists Urumqi, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shanghai among its Chinese connections. No operator has been named. A joint release said commercial and operational requirements will be discussed and the operator and launch schedule announced in the coming months.

Matteoni said a Nanjing link would strengthen options for businesses moving goods between the UK and one of China's largest provincial economies. Dai pointed to Jiangsu's substantial manufacturing base and two-way cargo flows.
stories.whyItMatters:
Read this as a signal about where UK air capacity is heading, not as a lane you can book. Prestwick already runs 20 China services a week, which tells you the airport has become a genuine alternative to Heathrow for ecommerce airfreight into the UK, particularly for sellers whose 3PL sits in Scotland or the north of England. A fifth Chinese gateway would spread your options across Jiangsu as well as Guangdong and Sichuan.

Jiangsu makes a large share of the consumer electronics, tools, textiles and homeware that UK sellers import. If a Nanjing route opens, a seller shipping 500kg a week out of Suzhou or Wuxi could truck to NKG in a few hours instead of running to PVG, and land at Prestwick rather than paying Heathrow handling. That is a real saving on drayage and airport charges, though nobody has published a rate.

Treat 2027 as a planning assumption only. No operator, frequency, cut-off or tariff exists yet. Keep your current gateway contracts and revisit when the operator is named.
stories.hotTake: Airport PR about routes that may open in 14 months is not capacity. Prestwick has done the hard part already with 20 weekly China services, and adding Nanjing is a sensible next step for a niche UK gateway. I would not move a single kilo of my Q1 volume on the strength of a handshake in Nanjing.
actions: Log Prestwick as a secondary UK gateway and check what your forwarder already quotes into PIK
Ask your Jiangsu suppliers which airport they truck to today and the drayage cost to NKG versus PVG
Revisit the lane when an operator and launch schedule are announced, not before

stories.headline: China's iron ore port stocks build to 149.13m tonnes
stories.tldr: Iron ore stocks at 35 major Chinese ports rose to 149.13 million tonnes on 6 November, up 1.08 million tonnes week-on-week.
stories.whatHappened:
Iron ore stocks at 35 major Chinese ports reached 149.13 million tonnes as of 6 November, up 1.08 million tonnes week-on-week, according to SMM. Arrivals fell markedly during the week, yet port stocks still built because outbound volumes weakened.

Average daily port outbound volume at the 35 ports fell 55,000 tonnes week-on-week to 3.12 million tonnes. Hot metal output at steel mills declined and outbound volumes fell with it. The most-traded I2701 contract on the Dalian Commodity Exchange closed at 687.5 yuan per tonne, up 0.07%. Spot prices for mainstream products at Qingdao port fell by about 3 yuan per tonne on average.

SMM said arrivals are expected to recover next week and port stocks may build further. It expects iron ore prices to turn range-bound at high levels in the short term.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you buy steel furniture, shelving, bike frames, tools, hardware, garden structures or anything with a steel content, this is your input cost signal. Port stocks at 149.13 million tonnes with weak mill offtake mean Chinese steel mills have ore sitting in front of them and soft demand behind them. That combination usually keeps domestic steel prices from spiking, which keeps your factory quotes stable through Q1.

The number to watch is mill maintenance. Hot metal output is already falling, and if mills extend maintenance through the winter heating season, spot steel supply tightens and your quotes move up. For a seller buying 20ft containers of steel-framed furniture, a 3 yuan per tonne move in Qingdao spot is noise. A mill maintenance wave is not.

This also matters for your freight planning. Weak steel demand means less bulk and breakbulk cargo moving through Chinese ports, which can free up berth windows for container vessels. That is a mild positive for schedule reliability on your sea freight.
stories.hotTake: 149 million tonnes sitting in Chinese ports with mills cutting output is a buyer's market for anyone sourcing steel. I would be asking my factory for a fixed quote through Q1 right now, before the winter maintenance season tightens spot supply. If they refuse, that tells you they expect prices to rise.
actions: Ask your steel-content suppliers for a fixed quote covering Q1 2027 while port stocks are high
Track Chinese mill maintenance announcements through November and December before committing to a spring price
If you buy steel-heavy SKUs, price a second order now rather than waiting for Chinese New Year quotes

stories.headline: China's AI chipmakers post first profits as memory costs bite
stories.tldr: Chinese GPU developers including Moore Threads, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX swung into profit in Q3, but memory costs threaten growth.
stories.whatHappened:
China's pure-play AI chipmakers crossed a profit milestone in the third quarter, with several domestic GPU developers swinging into profit, according to SCMP. The firms named include Moore Threads, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX, which are racing to fill the market gap left by Nvidia after US export controls restricted its high-end processors in China.

The same report flags severe supply chain hurdles and soaring memory costs as threats to long-term growth. The companies are competing hard for domestic customers and for access to advanced memory and packaging capacity.

A separate Menlo Ventures study found Chinese AI models accounted for 89% of global enterprise spending on open-source systems, with Moonshot AI's Kimi family leading at 61%.
stories.whyItMatters:
Two things here affect your cost base. First, soaring memory costs in China are not confined to AI chips. Memory feeds SSDs, USB drives, dashcams, security cameras, smart speakers, laptops and a long list of consumer electronics. If DRAM and NAND prices rise, your factory quotes for anything with storage inside them rise with it, usually with a one to two quarter lag.

Second, Chinese AI chipmakers competing for advanced packaging and memory capacity push up prices for everyone buying the same inputs. A seller sourcing smart home devices or computer peripherals should expect memory-driven cost increases in Q1 and Q2 2027 quotes, and should not assume a flat renewal from a supplier who has not yet repriced.

Ask your supplier directly what share of their bill of materials is memory and whether their memory supplier has issued a price increase notice. If they say yes, get the number and model it into your Q1 landed cost before you set retail prices.
stories.hotTake: Memory is the input cost nobody in ecommerce watches until it hits their quote. Chinese AI chip demand is soaking up domestic memory and packaging capacity, and that bill lands on every seller with a camera, a drive or a speaker in their catalogue. Ask for Q1 quotes now, in writing.
actions: Ask every electronics supplier what percentage of their BOM is memory and whether they have received a price increase notice
Pull Q1 2027 quotes forward to November and December while suppliers are still quoting 2026 prices
Model a 5% to 10% cost increase on storage-bearing SKUs and check your retail margin can absorb it

contentHooks: Prestwick is quietly building the UK's most interesting China air cargo network while everyone watches Heathrow
A fifth Chinese airport gateway into the UK is a drayage story, not a rate story, and drayage is where your margin hides
Iron ore sitting at 149 million tonnes in Chinese ports is your cue to lock Q1 steel quotes before winter maintenance
Memory costs are the input price increase ecommerce sellers will not see coming until their Q1 quote lands
Nobody is quoting rates on the Prestwick to Nanjing route because no operator has signed, and that is the point
If your supplier cannot tell you their memory cost exposure, they cannot protect your Q1 price
Steel-heavy SKUs are the easiest category to fix a price on right now, and almost nobody is doing it
The gap between a signed air route and an announced air route is where sellers get burned on capacity planning
Chinese AI chip profits are a supply chain signal for consumer electronics, not a tech story
Mill maintenance schedules in China move your furniture quote more than any freight rate this quarter
Twenty weekly China services into Prestwick already exist, so the story is not the future route, it is the current one

faq.question: Is there a direct cargo route from Nanjing to the UK yet?
faq.answer: No. Glasgow Prestwick and the Jiangsu Provincial Government are in talks about a Nanjing Lukou cargo connection with a possible 2027 launch, but no operator has been named and no schedule published. Prestwick currently handles 20 China services a week from Urumqi, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shanghai. Do not quote a Nanjing lane to a customer until an operator confirms it.

faq.question: Why are Chinese steel prices relevant to my product costs?
faq.answer: If your goods contain steel, Chinese mill pricing sets your factory quote. Iron ore stocks at 35 major Chinese ports hit 149.13 million tonnes on 6 November, up 1.08 million tonnes week-on-week, while daily outbound volumes fell to 3.12 million tonnes. High stocks and weak mill demand usually hold steel prices down. Watch mill maintenance, because extended maintenance tightens spot supply and lifts quotes.

faq.question: Will memory prices increase my electronics sourcing costs in 2027?
faq.answer: Likely yes. Chinese AI chipmakers are competing for advanced memory and packaging capacity, and reports flag soaring memory costs as a growth risk for those firms. Memory feeds SSDs, cameras, speakers and laptops, so factory quotes for storage-bearing products tend to rise with a one to two quarter lag. Ask suppliers what share of their bill of materials is memory and whether they have received a price increase notice.

faq.question: What is the best UK airport for China airfreight right now?
faq.answer: It depends on where your 3PL sits. Glasgow Prestwick already runs 20 weekly China services from Urumqi, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shanghai, which makes it a real alternative to Heathrow for sellers with UK fulfilment in Scotland or the north of England. Compare total cost including trucking to your warehouse, not just the airport-to-airport rate. Heathrow usually wins on frequency, Prestwick often wins on handling charges.
